approval_scope: Source reading of the PRAYER blocks 1, 3 and 5 on scan 8 only: block 1 from לְבָבֶֽךָ: to וּבִשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ:, block 3 from וְהָיָ֗ה to עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ:, and block 5 from וַיֹּ֥אמֶר to אֹתָ֑ם (Numbers 15:39, mid-verse). It combines the blind reading, the three v2 fine-image reports and the human answers 870–877 and 878–896.

findings.topic: Exactly 13 metegs added, and nothing else changed
findings.detail: I compared working/s8.json with reviewed_candidate_s8.json block by block. Block 1, the heading and both citations are identical. Block 3 has 10 additions, all U+05BD: w15 וְנָֽתַתִּ֧י on nun; w20 וְאָֽסַפְתָּ֣ on alef; w22 וְתִירֹֽשְׁךָ֖ on resh (host index 3, after the holam, not on tav); w24 וְנָֽתַתִּ֛י on nun; w26 בְּשָֽׂדְךָ֖ on sin; w28 וְאָֽכַלְתָּ֖ on alef; w35 וַֽעֲבַדְתֶּם֙ on the initial vav; w70 לְטֽוֹטָפֹ֖ת on the first tet (host index 1, not the vav or the second tet); w98 לַֽאֲבֹֽתֵיכֶ֖ם with two metegs, on lamed (index 0) and bet (index 2). Block 5 has 3 additions: w7 וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֣ on alef; w14 לְדֹֽרֹתָ֑ם on dalet (index 1, not lamed); w15 וְנָֽתְנ֛וּ on the first nun. Total: 10 + 3 = 13. I found no other change to consonants, vowels, accents or dagesh.

findings.topic: Occurrences bound to the right words
findings.detail: I counted the words independently from the start of blocks 3 and 5, treating maqaf-linked words as one unit. Every word_index in user_adjudications_878_896.json and questions_s8_final_pointing.json points to the intended word in the intended verse. Block 1's לְטֹטָפֹ֖ת (Deut 6:8) correctly has no meteg; q885 applies only to the Deut 11:18 occurrence at w70. The two ונתתי occurrences (w15 with darga, w24 with tevir) were each applied separately.

q881: אֹת֗וֹ (w24) has holam on alef, revia U+0597 on tav, and holam male on vav. q882: the lamed of לֵּאמֹֽר: keeps its dagesh. q886: the qadma U+05A8 in וּקְשַׁרְתֶּ֨ם (w65) is on tav (host index 4). This settles the closing report's provisional qadma-host limitation. q896: מָטָ֔ר (w46) has zaqef qatan U+0594 on tet. q894: וְלֹא־יִהְיֶ֣ה (w45) has no meteg. q895: אֶתְכֶ֖ם (w7) has no extra mark, and the record calls it a printing speck, not a sic/corr. Under the instructions' 'distinguish printing blemishes from actual marks' rule, it rightly gets no tei:choice.

findings.topic: q880 reconstruction from Miqra al pi ha-Masorah
findings.detail: numbers.xml line 135 (Numbers 15:39) reads וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם: patah on vav, hataf patah on ayin, hiriq on sin, segol plus tipcha on tav, and no meteg. Candidate w28 is the same. smudge_reconstruction records the URN, file, line, sha256 and the human's authorization, and states that this is a reconstruction of smudged pointing, not a claim that the print is clear and not a typo. That meets the instructions' requirement to record such reconstructions explicitly. Nothing nearby was imported from Miqra al pi ha-Masorah. The candidate keeps כָּל and מִצְוֹ֣ת where Miqra al pi ha-Masorah has כׇּל and מִצְוֺ֣ת. Miqra al pi ha-Masorah also has merkha in וְנָ֥תְנ֛וּ, but the candidate has the meteg the human confirmed.

findings.topic: Earlier human readings 870–877 and the occurrence correction are unchanged
findings.detail: All 870–872 marks in block 1 are present, including the meteg on the shuruq in וּֽבְשָׁכְבְּךָ֖ and the spelling מְזֻז֥וֹת. The 873–875 marks are present: וְהָיָ֗ה, שָׁמֹ֤עַ, תִּשְׁמְעוּ֙, מִצְוֹתַ֔י, הִשָּֽׁמְר֣וּ, and וְהָיָ֣ה לָכֶם֮ לְצִיצִת֒. So are 876 (וַיֹּ֥אמֶר, merkha on yod) and 877 (וַֽאֲבַדְתֶּ֣ם, w51). The s8_image_adjudications marks are present (w11, w16, w92, w93). The double pashta appears only on אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ (w44). הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם (w102) keeps tipcha only, which the closing report also confirmed from the image.

findings.topic: No mark is left provisional and unsettled
findings.detail: Every finding in the three v2 reports maps to a question that the human has now answered. That covers opening M1–M6 and U1–U4 (q887–896), closing M1, M2 and the qadma limitation (q884–886), and Numbers N1–N6 (q878–883). Where a report proposed a different host than the human gave, the human's answer was applied: opening M3 proposed tav and the meteg went on resh; closing M1 proposed bet or alef and the metegs went on lamed and bet.

findings.topic: A shallow check on the merkha in פֶּ֥ן
findings.detail: Opening report scope limitation 5 says the merkha under the pe of פֶּ֥ן־יִפְתֶּ֖ה (w32) was confirmed present but not examined closely, because the final-nun descender sits next to it. The reviewer saw no conflict. It is not marked provisional, and the host is not in doubt. I'm flagging it because you asked for every weakly checked item; I don't think it blocks approval. If you want it settled by a human, add one question.

findings.topic: The q878 question named only one possibility
findings.detail: q878 asked only whether there is a meteg on the first nun of וְנָתְנ֛וּ, and the human answered yes, so it is settled. For the record: Miqra al pi ha-Masorah has a merkha (U+05A5) in that position. I did not use that to second-guess the source, and the human's answer stands.

The method field ('fine marks are explicitly incomplete, not an accepted full pointing reading') and the uncertainties list were copied from the draft and are now outdated for blocks 1, 3 and 5. The q880 reconstruction evidence is recorded only in user_adjudications_878_896.json. Update or annotate these fields, and carry the reconstruction evidence into encoding, so later readers don't take the q880 pointing as clearly printed or the reading as unfinished.

scope_limitations: I compared the files visually in the Read tool output; I had no shell. I could not compute sha256 values (reviewed b9867985…, previous 4cf522d9…, current b6110898…) or list codepoints and their order byte by byte. Host letter and mark identity are verified from the rendered text. U+05BD is the only meteg/silluq codepoint, so I could not tell it from a lookalike, and I did not check mark order within letters, such as sin dot versus qamatz versus meteg in בְּשָֽׂדְךָ֖. Before encoding, run a mechanical diff that confirms exactly 13 U+05BD insertions and no other change, and check the hashes.
I did not view source images myself. Image evidence comes from the three v2 reports and the human answers.

The v2 fine-image reports cover only blocks 3 and 5 (rows 0–19, starting at Deut 11:13). For block 1 (Deut 6:6–9), approval rests on the blind reading plus human answers 870–872. I was not given a separate fine-image report for block 1.

Not accepted here: the whole page, the heading and citation blocks, JLPTEI encoding, Divine Name holam placement (an encoding convention, opening report limitation 4), canonical identity, alignment and order, encoding normalization, and exports.
Snippet preflight and question presentation (the instructions' question-before-snippet requirement) were not re-audited. Only the recorded snippet paths and hashes were seen.
